name: RT Lately
classification_notes: A contemporary sans built by tracing over a century of gothic letterform history, so it reads as a grotesque with historical detailing folded in rather than a plain neo-grotesque.
summary: A seven-weight grotesque that morphs a century of gothic letterform history into a single contemporary sans.
description: RT Lately treats gothic type history as source material, pulling naive early designs and timeless classics into one contemporary sans. Seven weights with matching italics give it real range for editorial and branding work that wants some historical grain.
foundry_blurb: RazziaType describe it as a time-traveling witness to the evolution of gothics, attesting to over a century of technological and stylistic transitions and shifting them back to the zeitgeist as a contemporary sans.

name: RT Dromo
classification_notes: An all-purpose grotesque modelled on 1980s concert-ticket typography, shipped with a matching monospaced cut.
summary: A vintage-ticket grotesque with the sturdiness of impact printing, shipped with a matching monospaced cut.
description: RT Dromo remixes 1980s concert-ticket typography into a contemporary, functionalist digital family. What began as a single custom weight has grown into seven weights with italics, plus a full monospaced companion.
foundry_blurb: RazziaType call it a typographic line-up of vintage concert ticket typography from the 1980s performed with the sturdiness of an all-purpose grotesque, echoing functionalist shapes proven in the challenging environments of impact printing.

name: RT Vitrine
classification_notes: A Didone-derived display face with its serifs cut away, leaving a high-contrast sans; classified as sans-serif because the foundry itself labels it a Display Sans.
summary: A high-contrast display sans that strips the serifs from a Didone skeleton for a crystalline, fashion-editorial look.
description: RT Vitrine started as an exploration of Didone display type and ended up somewhere else: serifs removed, stroke endings weightless, the letterforms reduced to a near see-through quality. Nine weights from Razor to Black give it real range for fashion and editorial display work.
foundry_blurb: RazziaType describe it as a high-contrast Display Sans achieving a see-through quality through formal reduction, an exploration into the field of display type and the Didone genre stripped back to its essence.

name: RT Rondelle
classification_notes: A grotesque built out of public-transport signage conventions, generalised into a consistent text-and-display family.
summary: A versatile grotesque built from public transport signage conventions, with a balanced geometrical touch.
description: RT Rondelle takes the DNA of transit signage typefaces and generalises it into a consistent eight-weight family, leaving the restrictions of its wayfinding heritage behind. It suits the same kind of clear, functional setting the source material was built for, plus general branding and text use.
foundry_blurb: RazziaType describe it as the result of an exploration into public transport signage typefaces, incorporating the distinctive characteristics of a highly specialised genre to become a versatile grotesque family with a balanced geometrical touch.

name: RT Alias
classification_notes: A pixel typeface system rooted in early screen-font aliasing, built on a sans-serif grotesque skeleton across four named subfamilies.
summary: A pixel-aliasing type system rooted in the technical limits of early on-screen font rendering, split across four subfamilies.
description: RT Alias rebuilds the visual glitches of early font aliasing on low-resolution screens into a deliberate typeface system. Four subfamilies (Grotesk, Fine, Medium and Rough), each in three weights with obliques, cover a wide range of retro-computing and screen-display use.
foundry_blurb: RazziaType root the idea in the technical constraints of font aliasing from when visual reproduction of fonts on screens was far less precise, calling it a highly versatile pixel typeface system with a changing grid and an additional sans-serif subfamily.
